comments.text_zh: 3Blue1Brown 对内在不确定性、以及它为何与测量不确定性相互独立，有一段极好的解释[1]。（上一集[2]是推荐的背景知识前置，讲傅里叶变换是如何工作的）> 通过另一种迄今未知的机制浮现出来。在 3Blue1Bron 的解释[1]中，他展示了内在不确定性是如何成为同时测量位置和频率时固有的权衡。一个只有几个波长长的短波包，对应着一个狭窄（精确）的位置范围，但由于其长度，也同样很好地对应着非常宽的频率范围。只要你处理的是长度接近波长的波包，就会存在类似海森堡式的不确定性。3Blue1Brown 用多普勒雷达给了一个很好的例子。[1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
comments.text: 3Blue1Brown has an extremely good explanation[1] of the intrinsic uncertainty, and why it's separate from measurement uncertainty. (the previous episode[2] is a recommended prerequisite for background on how the Fourier Transform works) > emerges through a different, as yet unknown, mechanism. In 3Blue1Bron's explanation[1], he shows how the intrinsic uncertainty is an inherent trade-off of trying to measure both position and frequency. A short wave packet only a few wavelengths long correlates with a narrow (precise) range of positions, but also correlates well with a very wide range of frequencies due. A Heisenberg-like uncertainty exists any time you are working with weave packets with length near the wavelength. 3Blue1Brown gives a very good example using Doppler radar. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 只是个小挑刺。作者在文章开头展示的那对公式并不是傅里叶变换及其逆变换的公式。傅里叶变换是一个作用于无限输入的连续函数。变换的公式涉及在 +/- 无穷上取积分。所展示的、使用求和符号的形式，是傅里叶变换的一种离散形式，其中输入是有限时间序列。可以在 Grant Sanderson 的 3 Blue 1 Brown 频道找到一个很好的替代解释 [VIDEO]
comments.text: Just a nit. The pair of equations the author showed at the beginning of the article are not the equations of the Fourier Transform and its inverse. The Transform is a continuous function operating on an infinite input. The equation for the Transform involves the use of the integral taken over +/- infinity. What is shown, using the summation operator, is a discrete form on the Transform where the input is a limited time series. A good alternative explanation can be found on Grant Sanderson's 3 Blue 1 Brown channel [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: Ask HN: What is your favourite tech talk?
comments.why_zh: 一长串推荐演讲清单中的一条。
comments.text_zh: Ted Nelson 的 Computers for Cynics 大概不包含对你们任何人来说新鲜的技术信息，但 Ted 有一种本事，能把事情重新框定，让某些历史决定的随意性变得一目了然：[LINK] 关于超文本这个话题，The Web That Wasn't 很好地梳理了这个想法的历史（适合那些以为它始于 TBL 的人——出乎意料地多！）：[LINK] 另一场以重新框定为核心的演讲是 Clay Shirky 的 "It's not information overload, it's filter failure"，它最终引向 Shirky 所建议的那类面向用户的过滤功能，也就是 Mastodon 已经实现的东西：[LINK] 在神经学与信息科学的交叉处，Peter Watts 总有些有趣的话要说，而作为一位研究海星神经系统的前海洋生物学家，这绝对正中他的老本行：[LINK] 这一场（"moving away from defensive programming"）相当清晰地论证了强类型的合理性：[LINK] 在元认知方面，Dan Dennett 和 Doug Hofstadter 一样有相关性：[LINK] Forgotten Ideas in Computer Science 开头比较慢，但如果你没有多少历史背景（比如，你对 70 年代计算机科学发生了什么只有模糊印象），它就是一长串清单，列着你在开始下一个项目之前应该去查一查、了解了解的东西：[LINK] 每个人都应该理解程序化生成：[LINK] 同样地，既然 AI 现在被吹得火热，我们都该提醒自己 IA 也是一回事：[LINK] Mo

comments.text: This is a combination of things that almost breaks my brain, but it works, and it's brilliant! First, you need to understand coded masks[1,2]. This is a way to use an LCD or other array to mask off parts of a scene so that very specific parts of it are sampled, but the rest aren't, to get a single, high resolution analog value. Then you switch to other masks, and get more values. You can then work backwards in the math through the known mask shapes, to get the original image with far fewer samples that would be required one at a time. Think of the above as a 2d visual version of the Fourier transform[3,4]. This transform is used heavily to compress images throwing away most of the bits in an image without losing it's essence. The analysis they're talking about uses a very specially printed card. It isn't just something generated with a standard 4 ink printer, each "dot" is a separate unique ink with tightly controlled spectral curves, these form a virtual version of the above masks. When you view these through a sample, it can then give an idea of the spectral response of the camera, and the liquid, by using the many different known response curves of the "dots" to work backwards, and generate the 1 dimensional very tight response curve of a hyperspectral imager, by figuring out where each "dot" is in the scene, then averaging that dot's intensity across the RGB values of the picture taken by the camera.
